Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome: absence of pubic and axillary hair
testes often in the abdomen or inguinal canals
5-Alpha Reductase Deficiency: at birth, the external genitalia may appear predominantly female or ambiguous
enlargement of the clitoris or phallus
Ovotesticular Disorder of Sex Developmen: mix of ovarian and testicular tissue
internal genitalia can include a combination of wolffian and müllerian structures
varied karyotype (46, XX; 46, XY; 46, XXY; or mosaicism)
46,XY Disorder of Sex Development: a group of conditions with normal male karyotype (46, XY) but disorder in sex development
can include various manifestations depending on the specific condition
Partial Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome: may have predominantly female, predominantly male, or ambiguous external genitalia
Hypospadias: urethral opening on the underside of the penis
can be isolated or part of a more complex disorder of sex development
Gonadal Dysgenesis: lack of development of the gonads
can be part of Turner syndrome (45, X) or other variations
Cryptorchidism: increased risk of testicular cancer and infertility
